orders.reason: endometriosis with worsening pain; trying to conceive about 10 months

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit, and she wants to talk about the endometriosis.

Since about the spring, the pain has stepped up: cramps now start a few days before her period and hang on through the last day of bleeding, and ibuprofen is not enough. Deep pain with intercourse is worse over the same six months. Cycles regular, about every 28 days, bleeding around five days.

They started trying again last December, about ten months without a pregnancy. She is ready to go back to gyn and hear the options, including surgery.

Meds: OTC ibuprofen with menses. NKDA.
PHQ-9: 3. Frustrated but coping; good support at home.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 23. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, mild lower abdominal tenderness, no mass, no guarding. Urine hCG negative.

A/P:
- Endometriosis with worsening pain while trying to conceive: re-referral to the same gynecology group so they can pick up where they left off in 2023.
- CBC and metabolic panel today.
- Flu and COVID today.
- Pap due next year.
- I'll watch for their letter.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 12/15/2025
Re: Melissa Nolan, DOB 12/09/1993

Ms. Nolan returns to our practice, last seen in June 2023, when her pelvic pain and difficulty conceiving were first evaluated and endometriosis was diagnosed on clinical grounds. She did not proceed with laparoscopy at that time.

She now has severe cramping pelvic pain that starts several days before menses and persists until bleeding stops. Deep dyspareunia has steadily worsened over the last six months. Cycles are regular, every 28 days with 5 days of flow. The couple has been trying to conceive for one year. She takes no medications at present.

Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with endometriosis; maternal aunt with infertility.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, elementary school teacher.

Exam: abdomen soft. Bimanual examination elicits tenderness; the uterus is retroverted and fixed. No adnexal mass is felt.

Labs drawn today: CBC, TSH with free T4, and prolactin, all within normal limits.

Assessment: secondary dysmenorrhea and deep dyspareunia due to endometriosis; one year of attempting conception.

Plan:
1. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily with food, starting a day or two before expected menses and through the heaviest days. Hormonal suppression is not appropriate while she is trying to conceive.
2. Return in about three weeks with pelvic ultrasound and further evaluation.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
PELVIC ULTRASOUND, TRANSABDOMINAL AND TRANSVAGINAL
Indication: endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain.
Uterus: normal in size. Endometrium normal in thickness. No focal myometrial lesion.
Ovaries: multiple cystic masses are present on both ovaries, each with diffuse low-level internal echoes giving a ground-glass appearance, without solid components or internal flow.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Multiple ground-glass cystic masses on both ovaries, in keeping with endometriomas. Normal-sized uterus.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 01/06/2026

Follow-up for endometriosis, seen here a month ago for severe menstrual cramps and before that for fertility concerns.

She describes six months of abnormal bleeding, which on questioning is spotting in the days before her period and heavier flow than she used to have; cycles remain regular. Periods continue to grow more painful, with pelvic discomfort between them and painful intercourse. Trying to conceive for about a year. Using naproxen with menses.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: uterus normal in size. Nodularity of the uterosacral ligaments.

CA-125: 61 U/mL (reference under 35), elevated.

Ultrasound today: multiple cystic ovarian masses bilaterally with a ground-glass appearance, consistent with endometriomas.

Assessment: endometriosis with bilateral ovarian endometriomas; the CA-125 elevation fits this picture.

Plan: return next month for a dedicated infertility evaluation. Continue naproxen.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
TRANSVAGINAL PELVIC ULTRASOUND
Indication: infertility, endometriosis.
Uterus: normal in size and contour. Endometrium normal for cycle day.
Left ovary: homogeneous hypoechoic cyst measuring 4.1 x 3.5 x 3.3 cm without internal flow or solid component.
Right ovary: no dominant cyst.
No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal-sized uterus. Homogeneous hypoechoic left ovarian cyst, 4.1 cm.

documents.title: Infertility Evaluation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Infertility consultation, 02/09/2026

Ms. Nolan comes back to our clinic to continue her infertility evaluation. Her earlier visits here were for chronic pelvic pain, severe dysmenorrhea and abnormal bleeding.

She and her partner have been attempting pregnancy for 14 months. Cycles come every 27 to 30 days and are reliably painful, most of all on the first two days of flow. She has intermittent lower abdominal discomfort that intensifies near her period. On direct questioning she notes occasional pain with deep penetration and some pelvic pain with bowel movements close to menses; she has had no rectal bleeding and no change in the caliber of her stools.

PSH: none; no abdominal surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: naproxen with menses.

Exam: mild tenderness with deep palpation of the posterior vaginal fornix.

Transvaginal ultrasound: normal-sized uterus; a homogeneous hypoechoic cyst on the left ovary.

Assessment: infertility of 14 months in a 32-year-old with endometriosis.

Plan:
1. Cervical NAAT for chlamydia and gonorrhea today.
2. Home urinary LH kits for the next several cycles to document ovulation.
3. Hysterosalpingogram in the follicular phase.
4. Endometrial biopsy in the luteal phase.
5. Semen analysis for her partner.
We will review everything together once complete.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: endometrium, office biopsy.
CLINICAL: infertility; biopsy timed to the luteal phase.
GROSS: received in formalin, multiple fragments of tan-red soft tissue, aggregate 1.5 cm, entirely submitted.
MICROSCOPIC: secretory endometrium with glandular and stromal features corresponding to the expected cycle day. No hyperplasia. No inflammation.
reports.conclusion: Secretory endometrium, in phase; consistent with normal luteal function.

documents.title: Infertility Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP
Office visit 06/15/2026

Returns to go over her infertility evaluation. Now 18 months of trying. Periods every 28 days for about 5 days. Lower abdominal pain with menses keeps getting worse, and deep dyspareunia continues. Naproxen helps somewhat.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: mild tenderness on deep palpation of the posterior fornix. No adnexal mass palpable. No cervical motion tenderness.

Results:
- Ovulation: confirmed on serial home urinary LH testing.
- Chlamydia and gonorrhea NAAT: negative.
- Hysterosalpingogram: normal uterine cavity, both tubes patent.
- Luteal endometrial biopsy: in phase, consistent with normal luteal function.
- Partner semen analysis: normal.

Assessment: 18 months of infertility with a normal basic evaluation; endometriosis is the likely contributor.

Plan: we discussed next steps, which range from assisted reproduction to surgery. I have referred her to reproductive endocrinology to review treatment options; their office will call to schedule. Continue naproxen as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.
